newsitem.title: INDIA: Commandos to guard Miss World contest in India.
newsitem.headline: Commandos to guard Miss World contest in India.

text.p: The Miss World beauty contest in India next month will be guarded by crack commandos and around 1,000 policemen to stop violent protests erupting, the police chief in the southern Indian city of Bangalore said on Monday.

The leader of a rural populist activist group called the Farmers Association, M.D. Nanjundaswamy, had threatened to torch the venue of the show, which he described as an example of "cultural imperialism."

Women activists from the Bangalore-based Mahila Jagarna (Forum to Awaken Women) have threatened that one member from the group will commit suicide by self-immolation on each of the 17 days leading up to the pageant.
The contest will be held on November 23.
India will be hosting the beauty pageant for the first time after a firm owned by Hindi film superstar Amitabh Bachchan secured contracts for the event.
Since then, various organisations have protested against the event, saying it degraded women and would insult Indian culture. The main focus of the anger is the swimsuit parade.
"How can the state survive if we give in to such pressure? I will see to it that lawless elements will be dealt with severely," police commissioner Sharat Chandra Burman told Reuters.

He said more than 1,000 policemen, including commandos from the rapid action force, will be guarding the Chinnaswamy cricket stadium in the heart of the Karnataka state capital, where the event will be staged.
"We are drawing up a massive security plan. Participants from different countries will be given adequate protection," Burman said.
Nanjundaswamy and his supporters have attacked multi-national fast food outlets in the past in a campaign against multinationals operating in the food sector.
Nanjundaswamy and 40 supporters were arrested after ransacking a branch of the U.S. chain Kentucky Fried Chicken early this year.

"He is in the habit of giving a call for violence. Law enforcement (officials) are fully aware of his gimmicks. There may be protests here and there but it will not affect the show from being held," the police chief said.

At one protest on Monday a crowd in the town of Sirsi, in Karnataka, marched under the banner "Anti-Beauty Contest Committee" and burnt effigies of the state's chief minister J.H. Patel and Amitabh Bachchan.

Pramilla Nesargi, a legislator for the Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party, India's main opposition party, was among the first to raise her voice against the beauty contest coming to India. She is continuing to keep up the offensive.
"We are against the concept itself. The swimsuit is just a part of the culture we are opposed to," she said.
"You can't treat a woman as an exhibit," Nesargi said.
